amazon.name: Amazon
amazon.key_insight: Amazon is the most commercially successful behavioral design in history — and the most ethically polarized. One-click buy genuinely reduces friction. Prime genuinely provides value. But the same behavioral toolkit that makes buying easy makes canceling hard. Amazon proves that behavioral design is morally neutral: identical techniques (friction manipulation, default exploitation, cognitive load management) create user value when applied to purchasing and destroy user autonomy when applied to retention. The regulatory response (FTC lawsuit, EU DSA) suggests that the market is beginning to price in behavioral design ethics.
amazon.top_technique: One-Click Buy: The Friction Elimination Patent

slack.name: Slack
slack.key_insight: Slack is the clearest example of how behavioral design optimized for engagement metrics can directly conflict with user wellbeing in a workplace context. The green dot creates surveillance anxiety, channel proliferation fragments attention, and notification urgency turns every message into a potential trigger. The product works brilliantly for Slack's business (more messages = more 'engaged' = easier enterprise renewal) but actively undermines the deep work that knowledge workers are ostensibly paid to do. Slack proves that 'engagement' as a success metric can be actively harmful when the user's goal isn't entertainment but productive work.
slack.top_technique: The Green Dot: Presence as Social Control
